findings.title: len<4 fragment heuristic false-positives on 3-letter acronyms
findings.observation: W3 replay shows 4 fragment-like route labels vs 2 in Wave 2 under the same diagnostic rule: NAV (routing/ROUT-040, safety/SAF-009) and URL (routing/ROUT-072, routing/ROUT-083).
findings.classification: diagnostic-only heuristic false positive, not a gate and not a product regression: NAV is a legitimate 3-letter service acronym and these routes are new structured outputs that appeared because route construction now works; JUNK_ROUTE_PASS gate = 0 in both waves
findings.disposition: no runtime change in Wave 3; a future harness/contract task may add an explicit acronym allowlist (e.g. NAV) to the fragment diagnostic rule
findings.wave2_comparison: URL labels (ROUT-072, ROUT-083) are pre-existing Wave-2 lexical-fallback junk, unchanged in kind; ROUT-072 also dropped its former Hensikt heading fragment, an improvement

findings.title: URL fragment labels from lexical fallback (pre-existing)
findings.observation: routing/ROUT-072 and routing/ROUT-083 carry URL route labels from the RC-07 quoted/bold lexical fallback.
findings.classification: pre-existing Wave-2 behavior, not a Wave-3 regression; structural-only observation
findings.disposition: deferred; candidate for a future lexical-fallback guard task if Measurement V3 shows semantic impact

findings.title: family-law doc-26 section-8 table minting ceiling
findings.observation: structured extraction validates service names against a frozen header whitelist {instans, tjeneste, service}; doc-26 family-law rows live under a section-8 table whose header does not include a whitelisted identity term, so those rows cannot mint route targets.
findings.classification: deliberate fail-closed ceiling: header whitelist was frozen without tilbud because doc 25 commune tables would mint municipality names; extending it risks re-opening junk/fragment gates
findings.disposition: documented ceiling; any whitelist extension requires its own bounded task with header-safety analysis

findings.title: row-prefix access-marker ceiling
findings.observation: self-referral hints are derived from positive self-contact markers and negative/positive outranking patterns at claim level; row cells whose access semantics are encoded only as row prefixes are not parsed.
findings.classification: bounded simplification, fail-closed to UNCLEAR access state which the spec explicitly allows
findings.disposition: no Wave-3 change; potential future bounded access-path extraction task

findings.title: header whitelist frozen without tilbud
findings.classification: frozen design decision, prevents doc-25 commune-table minting
findings.disposition: recorded; revisit only with dedicated header-safety analysis

zero_open_hard_gates: all hard mechanism gates PASS; findings above are ceilings and diagnostics, not gate failures
